patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] mm/hmm: reject shadow-stack mappings
patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch rejects shadow-stack mappings in the Heterogeneous Memory Management (HMM) module to prevent devices from gaining write access to user-space shadow stacks on x86 architectures.

review_comments.author: Jason Gunthorpe
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Jason Gunthorpe noted that pte_write() incorrectly returns true for shadow-stack PTEs, which can lead to devices gaining write access when they shouldn't, and suggested introducing a new function like pte_real_write() to accurately report the write bit.
review_comments.raw_body:
Bah, it's not writable at all. The CPU PTE has write disabled and
someone thought it was a good idea to make pte_write() return true
because the CPU allows writes through a special instruction on this
special PTE? So now all the places like this think its writable, when
it really isn't.

You could also fix this by having something like pte_real_write() or
whatever that doesn't lie about the write bit in the PTE :|

The patch is still fine, in that it matches what everything else does,
but I'd include these details someplace..

Jason

review_comments.author: Andrew Morton
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted that on x86, shadow-stack PTEs have their write bit clear but pte_write() reports them writable due to special instructions, allowing GPU access and potential corruption of return addresses or bypassing protection; requested rejecting shadow-stack VMAs in hmm_vma_walk_test() including read access
review_comments.raw_body:
How does this look for an altered changelog?

: On x86, a shadow-stack PTE has its ordinary write bit clear.  The CPU
: rejects ordinary stores to it, but pte_write() reports it writable because
: shadow-stack instructions can write it.  HMM consequently sets
: HMM_PFN_WRITE, which Nouveau turns into ordinary GPU write permission.  A
: process with GPU access can then overwrite its own shadow stack,
: potentially corrupting return addresses or bypassing that protection.
: 
: Reject shadow-stack VMAs in hmm_vma_walk_test(), including read access.  A
: requested fault returns -EFAULT; a snapshot records HMM_PFN_ERROR.

I completely missed this, that will teach me to trust pte_write() I

or rename pte_write() to pte_fake_write() instead and restore

review_comments.author: David (Arm)
review_comments.summary: reviewer noted that pte_write() is sufficient for core-mm's needs, and that nobody besides selected core-mm code should write to random PTEs; they suggested using GUP instead of reimplementing it in HMM
review_comments.raw_body:
It's writable by the hardware, that's what matters to core-mm, for example, when
it comes to things like fork(), mproetect() etc.

*nobody* besides selected core-mm code should ever write to random PTEs. They
shouldn't ever even care about pte_write().

We have GUP for that, which takes care of that oddity properly when deciding
whether we can *actually* write to a mapped page.

Well, and we have HMM that reimplements part of GUP in ugly ways (sorry) that we
missed.

-- 
Cheers,

David

review_comments.author: Andrew Morton
review_comments.summary: reviewer noted that on x86, shadow-stack PTEs have their ordinary write bit clear but pte_write() reports them writable due to shadow-stack instructions; this allows HMM to grant devices write access to the process's shadow stack, potentially corrupting return addresses or bypassing protection
review_comments.raw_body:
Thanks.  This?

On x86, a shadow-stack PTE has its ordinary write bit clear.  The CPU
rejects ordinary stores, but pte_write() reports it writable because
shadow-stack instructions can write it.  HMM consequently sets
HMM_PFN_WRITE.  Nouveau uses that flag for GPU write permission, and
RDMA on-demand paging can use it to grant device write permission to a
registered memory region.  A device, or an RDMA peer with write access
to that region, can then overwrite the process's shadow stack,
potentially corrupting return addresses or bypassing that protection.

Reject shadow-stack VMAs in hmm_vma_walk_test(), including read access.
A requested fault returns -EFAULT; a snapshot records HMM_PFN_ERROR.

review_comments.author: Jason Gunthorpe
review_comments.summary: reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where a device gains ordinary write access to a shadow stack, which can lead to unexpected behavior
review_comments.raw_body:
Sure, thanks

Jason

review_comments.author: Alistair Popple
review_comments.summary:
reviewer pointed out that they had previously asked the HMM question on a different thread, and requested clarification on why it was being addressed in this patch

reviewer pointed out that the patch's assumption about shadow-stack mappings being universally writable by HW is incorrect, as _PAGE_RW = 0 and pte_write() returns true for logically writable pages
review_comments.raw_body:
Yeah, I asked the HMM question there -
https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/avT2FNTZoEuijEZP@nvdebian.thelocal/

---

Except they're not universally writable by HW, after all _PAGE_RW = 0. So
pte_write() is documented to return if it is logically writable, which of course
is what hmm_range_fault() also needs for certain values of "logic" :-)

So it's easy to see how this is confusing and got missed. Anyway this fix looks
good:

Reviewed-by: Alistair Popple <apopple@nvidia.com>

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 0/3] mm: fix swapcache writeout and cluster table races

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 0/3] mm: fix swapcache writeout and cluster table races

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] mm: vmscan: allow writeout of swapcache folios without anon mappings
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows the writeout of swapcache folios without anonymous mappings, enabling reclaim to write out dirty pages in swapcache even if they don't have an anonymous mapping. This is necessary because pageout() previously rejected these pages before they could be written out using the existing swap writeout path. The change affects how the filesystem checks for valid mappings and allows swapcache folios to bypass certain checks.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] mm/swap: publish cluster tables after reacquiring allocator locks
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a memory pressure scenario where the swap cluster population table is published while its locks are dropped, allowing it to be consumed and freed by another allocator before the original allocator resumes. To prevent this, the patch ensures that the cluster tables are kept private until they are fully restored after reacquiring all allocator locks. This approach maintains the integrity of the cluster allocation process and prevents potential data corruption or inconsistencies.

review_comments.author: Kairui Song
review_comments.summary: Gave Acked-by

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] mm/swap: skip relocation of tableless clusters
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a bug in the swap cluster relocation logic, where a stale reclaimer can free a tableless cluster while another allocator is still populating its table. The fix involves skipping relocation of clusters without tables to prevent dereferencing NULL pointers and potential FREE-to-NONE state cycles.

review_comments.author: Kairui Song
review_comments.summary: Agreed with the fix and acknowledged it as a valid solution to prevent dereferencing NULL pointers. Suggested that the patch is similar in intent to the 'discarding' status comment.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 11:14 PM Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> A stale reclaimer can reach relocate_cluster() after another allocator
> re-isolates an emptied cluster and drops its locks to populate the table.
> The cluster has zero count, CLUSTER_FLAG_NONE and no table, so relocation
> can free it again and dereference NULL in the DEBUG_VM empty check.
>
>     CPU0                                    CPU1
>     Reclaimer                               Allocator
>     alloc_swap_scan_cluster()
>       cluster_reclaim_range()
>         spin_unlock(&ci->lock)
>         __try_to_reclaim_swap()
>           swap_cache_del_folio()
>             __swap_cache_del_folio()
>               __swap_cache_do_del_folio()
>                 __swap_cluster_free_entries()
>                   free_cluster()
>                     __free_cluster()
>                       swap_cluster_free_table()
>             swap_cluster_unlock(ci)
>                                             isolate_lock_cluster()
>                                               swap_cluster_populate()
>                                                 drop ci and outer locks
>                                                 swap_cluster_alloc_table()
>         spin_lock(&ci->lock)
>       relocate_cluster()
>         free_cluster()
>           __free_cluster()
>             swap_cluster_assert_empty()
>               __swap_table_get()  /* NULL table */
>
> Leave tableless clusters to the allocator under ci->lock. This also stops
> a stale reclaimer from returning a cluster to the free list while table
> population is pending, avoiding the resulting FREE-to-NONE state cycle.
> The existing cluster lock serializes the table check and relocation with
> population.
>
> Reported-by: Sashiko <sashiko-bot@kernel.org>
> Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/sashiko-outbox-203018@kernel.org/
> Fixes: 07adc4cf1ecd ("mm, swap: implement dynamic allocation of swap table")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Signed-off-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>
> ---
>  mm/swapfile.c | 7 +++++++
>  1 file changed, 7 insertions(+)
>
> diff --git a/mm/swapfile.c b/mm/swapfile.c
> index 32639f65f13c..9fd62e4ca7a0 100644
> --- a/mm/swapfile.c
> +++ b/mm/swapfile.c
> @@ -815,6 +815,13 @@ static void relocate_cluster(struct swap_info_struct *si,
>         if (cluster_is_discard(ci))
>                 return;
>
> +       /*
> +        * An allocator may still be preparing the table.
> +        * Leave the cluster to it.

It's more like the cluster is in an "isolated" state so we shouldn't
touch it, similar to the "discarding" status above, this comment also
looks to me. Huge thanks for fixing this!

> +        */
> +       if (!cluster_table_is_alloced(ci))
> +               return;
> +
>         if (!ci->count) {
>                 if (ci->flags != CLUSTER_FLAG_FREE)
>                         free_cluster(si, ci);
> --
> 2.53.0-Meta
>

Acked-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] mm: mglru: splice all generations when reparenting a memcg

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm: mglru: splice all generations when reparenting a memcg

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a list_del corruption issue in the Linux kernel's memory management system (mm) by splicing all generations of MGLRU lists when reparenting a memcg (memory control group). The problem occurs when a memcg goes offline and its MGLRU lists are moved to the parent, but only certain generations are moved. This can lead to a folio being left on a freed memcg, causing a use-after-free error. To fix this, the patch moves all MAX_NR_GENS lists, not just those from min_seq to max_seq, ensuring that all folios are properly reparented and avoiding the corruption issue.

review_comments.author: Kairui Song
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that FG's folio_inc_lru_refs may cause a race between aging and lazy promotion, potentially landing a folio in a stall gen list, but agreed that this issue is not critical and can be addressed separately.

Reviewer Kairui Song agrees that the patch improves safety and cleanliness of the code
review_comments.raw_body:
Thanks for looking into this!

FG needed that because FG's folio_inc_lru_refs is a generic MGLRU
lockless lazy promotion, it may cause race between aging & lazy
promotion, landing a folio in a stall gen list. This isn't a big
problem, the worst outcome is a hotness inversion, which happens
almost once in a million times.

And right as Shakeel pointed out the problem already exists for
reparenting and lazy promotion, so we can fix it first.

---

Landing this one first is totally fine by me. The code is actually
safer and cleaner, in my opinion, with this patch.

Reviewer Kairui Song pointed out that the description of sort_folio() behavior in the patch is inaccurate, as MAX_NR_GENS - MIN_NR_GENS equals 2, and a stale gen can be outside the range [min_seq, max_seq].

Reviewer Kairui Song noted that this patch is similar to a previous commit for MGLRU-FG, which is a clean fix, but was surprised the problem was already reproducible.

"sort_folio() puts the folio on the list for max_seq + 1" seems not

The fix itself looks good.

---

As Barry mentioned this is basically the same code as a prepare commit
for MGLRU-FG, which is a fine and clean fix, I just didn't realize the

Thanks!
